receipt.public_excerpt: The S-1’s statements run to June 30, and the third quarter’s dollars are blank where the risk factors give the growth from $197 million.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows the S-1 financial statements stop at Q2 and the Q3 revenue figure is blank, given only as a multiple. This matches 'left out the majority of its Q3 numbers'.

evidence_items.locator: section 'The quarters, and the one in ratio form', paragraph 4

receipt.public_excerpt: That is growth of about 45 to 48 percent on the second quarter, and about $5.2 billion to $5.6 billion added, the first quarter in the series to add fewer dollars than the one before.

evidence_items.explanation: Q3 growth of about 45-48% compares with 144.2% in Q2 (same source), and Q3 added fewer dollars than Q2. Growth began to slow right after the last reported quarter.

metric_scope.metric: Quarterly revenue growth, quarter on quarter

inputs: Q3 2026 revenue = 86 x Q4 2024 revenue of $197 million (S-1)
derived.rounding: About 45-48% once rounding of the 86x multiple is allowed for

receipt.public_excerpt: $114.5bn to Google through July 2033, $110bn to Amazon through April 2036 and $44.9bn to Microsoft through May 2033, “regardless of actual usage”. It has also committed to $161.2bn in five-year equipment leases with Broadcom, excluding interest. Neither party can cancel the leases, and most of the capacity is due to come online from 2027.

evidence_items.explanation: The four non-cancellable deals sum to $430.6 billion, which is over $430 billion. The largest, Broadcom, mostly comes online from 2027, so the commitments start after the reported quarter.

receipt.public_excerpt: At the end of June, it had signed $321.4bn of compute and infrastructure leases that had yet to begin, up from $50.2bn six months earlier, and they are due to start between 2026 and 2028.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that a large share of committed compute had not yet started as of the last reported quarter and runs from 2026 to 2028. This supports 'before ... begin to kick in'.

unresolved_gaps: The S-1 itself could not be read directly (SEC returned 403). The figures come from close secondary readings with section citations.
The S-1 does give some Q3 metrics (customer counts, net revenue retention of about 900%, the 86x revenue multiple, top-five share for nine months). 'Majority' is a judgement call.
Part of the Google, Amazon and Microsoft cloud commitments is already being paid. 'Begin to kick in' fits the bulk of new capacity, not every dollar.
